item.title: How Raúl Castro’s Grandson, Raúl G. Rodríguez Castro, Became a Power Broker
item.description: The Castro family envoy, Raúl G. Rodríguez Castro, who has been in talks with the Trump administration, was once named in a case targeting a Cuban smuggling ring.

item.media:description: Raúl Castro, with his grandson and bodyguard Raúl G. Rodríguez Castro, during an official ceremony in Paris in 2016.

item.title: What to Know About the Cuban Mafia in Quintana Roo
item.description: A group of Cuban men in Mexico was charged with smuggling people to the United States. One of its leaders said Raúl Castro’s grandson helped, according to interviews and court records.
item.dc:creator: David C. Adams and Frances Robles
item.media:credit: Jae C. Hong/Associated Press
item.media:description: The former Los Angeles Dodgers player Yasiel Puig was one of the Cubans smuggled into the United States by a criminal group known as the Cuban Mafia.

item.title: Democrats Plan New Push to Defeat Max Miller in Ohio After Abuse Accusations
item.description: The party’s congressional campaign arm added Mr. Miller’s opponent, Brian Poindexter, to its highly competitive “Red to Blue” list.
item.dc:creator: Emily Davies
item.media:credit: Daniel Lozada for The New York Times
item.media:description: Brian Poindexter is the type of candidate Democrats believe can win over working-class voters who have flocked to President Trump in recent years.

item.title: How We’re Covering an ‘Identity Crisis’ in Politics
item.description: Recent primary wins have posed critical questions for both Republicans and Democrats as they head into the fall midterms. Carolyn Ryan, managing editor of The New York Times, shares how reporters approach coverage of shifting political dynamics.

item.title: Will the Left Keep Winning in the Midwest? What to Watch in Tuesday’s Primaries.
item.description: The left and the middle continue to battle in Democratic primaries for governor in Wisconsin and Senate in Minnesota. In South Carolina, all eyes are on Darline Graham.
item.dc:creator: Patricia Mazzei
item.media:credit: Alex Kent/The New York Times
item.media:description: Senator Darline Graham, who was appointed to complete the remainder of the late Senator Lindsey Graham’s term, is also running to succeed her brother for a full term. She faces four others in the special Republican primary.

item.title: Will Wisconsin Voters Think Francesca Hong Is Too Radical? Here’s Where She Stands.

item.media:description: Francesca Hong at a candidate forum in Prairie du Sac, Wis., in July.

item.title: A Syrian Holdout Province, Sweida, Fears a Government Takeover

item.dc:creator: Nanna Heitmann and Abdi Latif Dahir
item.media:description: Gunmen swept into southern Syria last year, setting off one of the deadliest bouts of sectarian violence in years.

item.title: Homeland Security Intensifies Pursuit of Noncitizens on Voter Rolls
item.description: Immigrants who said they inadvertently registered to vote while obtaining or renewing driver’s licenses are increasingly facing deportation under the Trump administration.

item.media:credit: Nick Hagen for The New York Times
item.media:description: In the past, the Homeland Security Department has not aggressively tried to deport the relatively small number of noncitizens who unlawfully registered to vote.

item.title: How Social Media Sparked a Refugee Crisis Between Spain and Morocco

item.description: Rumors swirled that Morocco, perhaps spurred by Israel and the United States, organized a recent border disaster. That unproven speculation, experts said, was exacerbated by the region’s complicated history.
item.dc:creator: Jason Horowitz
item.media:credit: Finbarr O'Reilly for The New York Times
item.media:description: Migrants from sub-Saharan Africa waiting on a beach for humanitarian assistance after about tens of thousands of people, mostly from Morocco, surged across the border into Ceuta, Spain, this month.
